item.title: One Piece: 5 Overpowered Devil Fruits Too Broken For The Canon Anime
item.description:
Eiichiro Oda got so many things right when creating One Piece , but Devil Fruit might be his greatest stroke of genius. Allowing for almost any ability, the power system gives the mangaka ultimate freedom to go wild, though Oda set a few rules to keep things balanced within the canon. OP Devil Fruits exist in One Piece , but if you want to see some truly cheat-code powers, you need to look at One Piece 's games.

Console and handheld games have introduced original Devil Fruits that prioritize boss battles over fitting into the overall universe, resulting in a few world-breaking mechanics that run counter to One Piece 's established lore, stakes, and scaling. Aside from appearing in filler arcs that might as well be make-believe, these broken Devil Fruits will never be canon in the manga or anime.

While I'm focusing on Devil Fruits introduced in One Piece games, I have made a single exception.

5 Simon's Pasa Pasa no Mi (Paper-Paper Fruit)

Yes, Paper Can Be Mightier Than Sand (Or Fire, Lightning, And Rubber)

  • Introduced in One Piece: Great Hidden Treasure of the Nanatsu Islands
  • Devil Fruit Type: Logia
  • The Power: A Logia-class fruit that allows Simon to transform his body into paper or manipulate it at will.

I know what you are thinking: How is Simon's Paper-Paper Fruit any different from Crocodile or Luffy's Devil Fruits? Surely, this ability would fit neatly into the canon story.

On paper (pun completely intended), the Pasa Pasa no Mi sounds weak and uninspired, but Simon uses it in ways that are completely busted. In addition to transforming into sheets or shards of paper, which allow him to fly or mitigate damage, Simon can also write symbols that grant unique abilities . He can create multiple explosions, heal his health, improve his reflexes, or generate new types of attacks.

Want a prime example of this Devil Fruit's absurd potential? Paper's natural enemy is fire, and Simon is certainly vulnerable to a surprise cooking; however, he can simply write that fire doesn't hurt him to negate that damage. Logia users typically don't have any regenerative abilities either, but Simon can heal his wounds fairly easily.

Great Hidden Treasure of the Nanatsu Islands seem to be set just before the Arabasta arc and Crocodile's introduction as One Piece 's strongest villain at the time. Simon's Devil Fruit is way more versatile and powerful than Crocodile's Suna Suna no Mi .

4 Eldoraggo's Goe Goe no Mi (Scream-Scream Fruit)

An OP Spammable Long-Range Energy Railgun

  • Introduced in One Piece: The Movie and One Piece: Become the Pirate King!
  • Devil Fruit Type: Paramecia
  • The Power: Converts sound into beams of energy
  • Yes, Eldoraggo is the exception, as he debuts in One Piece: The Movie . However, he also appears in One Piece: Become the Pirate King! , which came out just a few months after the film.

I mean, just look at the above picture! Eldoraggo's Devil Fruit turns him into a Dragon Ball character , as he basically just fires out the Mouth Energy Wave used by the likes of Piccolo or Nappa. In the movie, he doesn't overuse his Devil Fruit, but there's nothing to suggest it requires great physical effort or a cooldown period; he just screams and blasts everything away.

Eldoraggo's Goe Goe no Mi would work as a late-story Devil Fruit, but it has absolutely no business appearing on an East Blue villain. Due to showing up so early, the anime neutered the ability's impact by giving it a Luffy-centric weakness that lets the Straw Hats bounce a beam back to its sender.

3 Noko's Nemuri Nemuri no Mi (Sleep-Sleep Fruit)

If Freddy Krueger Was A One Piece Seahorse

  • Introduced in One Piece: Ocean's Dream!
  • Appears in the anime's Ocean's Dream Arc, a filler storyline
  • Devil Fruit Type: Paramecia
  • The Power: Traps people in their dreams and can even manipulate memories.


Don't be fooled by his adorable appearance; Noko is a cruel-as-heck seahorse who possesses a truly horror-worthy ability . The Nemuri Nemuri no Mi unleashes a mist that causes enemies to sleep, which is a pretty basic concept; however, the Devil Fruit also lets Noko erase or rewrite that person's long-term memories.

In Ocean's Dream and its remake, Dragon's Dream , Noko knocks the Straw Hats out and then erases their memories of who they are, what they can do, and what they mean to each other. Mechanically, this concept strips Luffy and the crew of their fighting acumen, allowing the game to introduce a traditional progression system. Narratively, Noko's Devil Fruit is pure nightmare fuel that could change the entire world , and Doflamingo takes over an island using Sugar's similar ability.

Noko's Devil Fruit is even stronger than Sugar's because it doesn't require direct contact and carries far less physical risk.

2 Pato's Inu Inu no Mi, Model: Bake-danuki (Mythical Tanuki Fruit)

Creates Perfect Clones Of Seemingly Everything

  • Introduced in One Piece: Unlimited World Red
  • Devil Fruit Type: Mythical Zoan
  • The Power: Transforms the user into a raccoon dog, granting them the ability to transform leaves into people, objects, or even environments

Pato's Inu Inu no Mi, Model: Bake-danuki is the perfect video game Devil Fruit , as it allows One Piece: Unlimited World Red to introduce popular villains and characters without having to justify their presence. Mythical Zoans are, by definition, rare and incredibly strong, but Pato takes things to a whole other level that simply cannot exist within the main story.

Although their power varies, Pato creates near-perfect clones of Hody Jones, Whitebeard, Ace, Warpol, Rob Lucci, Akainu, and even Blackbeard. All he needs to do is write down their name on a leaf, and they come alive with their Devil Fruit powers intact. He even creates a simultaneous army of One Piece 's strongest characters, although they end up being far weaker than his single clones.

1 Patrick Redfield's Bato Bato no Mi, Model: Vampire (Bat-Bat Fruit, Model: Mythical Vampire)

Infinite Youth And Immortality Achieved Through Combat

  • Introduced in One Piece: Unlimited World Red
  • Devil Fruit Type: Mythical Zoan
  • The Power: Vampire

I don't know; One Piece incorporating supernatural archetypes like vampires feels strange, like the concept doesn't belong in the universe. Frankly, Unlimited World Red mostly succeeds at reinforcing that perception through Patrick Redfield, an ancient pirate who is pretty much a straightforward vampire. Along with other stuff, this includes an ability to regain his youth by sucking someone's life force, effectively overcoming mortality.

Brook's Yomi Yomi no Mi is probably the closest canon Devil Fruit, as it revives him and keeps him from aging; however, he can easily die and doesn't have a slew of other OP abilities. For the most part , One Piece preserves the threat of natural physical degradation, old age, and disease, and it certainly wouldn't pair immunity with stats comparable to those of Gol D. Roger and Whitebeard.

item.title: July 9 is a Super Busy Day for PS5 Gamers
item.description:
The summer months may be the slowest when it comes to new video game releases, but that doesn't mean there still isn't plenty on the way for the PlayStation 5 in the very near future. The PlayStation 5 is one of the most popular video game platforms in the world, and so it make sense that nearly all major games are released on it.

The PS5 gets its own exclusive games, plus nearly all big multi-platform, third-party releases. This ensures that there are constantly new games released on the PS5, so gamers on the platform always have something new to play. PS5 gamers looking for something new to play in July should take note of the games releasing this month, with July 9 set to be a particularly busy day for the console.

New PS5 Games Coming on July 9

  • Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
  • Backyard Baseball
  • EA Sports College Football 27
  • Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok
  • Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avengers iX 1+2 Dual Collection

On July 9, PS5 gamers will be able to check out Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced , Backyard Baseball , EA Sports College Football 27 , Granblue Fantasy: Relink - Endless Ragnarok , and Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avengers iX 1+2 Dual Collection . July 9 is easily going to be the busiest day in July for PS5 gamers looking for a new game to play, as two of the month's biggest releases are dropping on that day.

Upcoming Releases

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a remake of Assassin's Creed 4: Black Flag , considered to be one of the best entries in Ubisoft's long-running franchise. Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced looks to bring AC4 's open world pirate experience to modern platforms with improved graphics and some new content. There's a great deal of hype for Black Flag Resynced among nostalgic gamers, and its release alone should ensure that July 9 is a busy day for the PS5.

EA Sports College Football 27 , meanwhile, is also doing a lot of work to make July 9 one to watch for PS5 gamers. After a decade of no new game releases, EA revived its college football franchise with the well-reviewed EA Sports College Football 25 . That game was followed up by EA Sports College Football 26 the next year, and now it's EA Sports College Football 27 's turn. While it likely won't feel nearly as fresh as 25 or even 26 , College Football 27 should prove to be yet another solid iteration of the franchise. And if it's anything like the previous games in the series, chances are it will be one of the best-selling new video game releases of the year by the time it's all said and done.

Halo: Campaign Evolved is coming to PS5 on July 28, marking the first time ever that a Halo game has released for a PlayStation console. Campaign Evolved is a remake of the original Halo: Combat Evolved , and it should be a perfect jumping-on point for PS5 gamers, even though it's missing its iconic multiplayer mode.

item.title: 1,226 Piece LEGO E.T. Set Officially Revealed
item.description:
LEGO has officially announced its long-expected E.T. set. Based on Steven Spielberg's iconic 1982 film, LEGO's latest licensed product is scheduled to launch later in summer 2026.

As is often the case with the company's models, LEGO's E.T. set leaked before its announcement, including through a packaging photo. However, even that leak did not fully spoil the set's key selling point: its immense posing potential.

LEGO Unveils Remarkably Posable E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial Set

Announced on July 3, LEGO's new E.T . set immortalizes the titular extraterrestrial with a large brick-built replica that is highly posable, even by the Danish toymaker's flagship product standards. The 1,226-piece build features a fully articulated neck that can rotate 360 degrees, a mouth that opens, and detailed arms with rotating shoulders and articulated wrists and fingers. Identified by product number 21370, the E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial set is scheduled for release as part of LEGO's August 1 wave.

New LEGO E.T. Set Overview

  • Theme : LEGO Ideas
  • Product No. : 21370
  • Name : E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
  • Pieces : 1,226
  • Age rating : 18+
  • Price : $139.99
  • Release : August 1, 2026
  • Pre-orders . LEGO

Beyond its articulation, the model includes several display features that recreate some of the most recognizable imagery from Spielberg’s iconic film. E.T. can be posed with an extended finger, referencing the famous "phone home" gesture, while the included pot of sunflowers nods to the scene in which he revives the wilting flowers. The set costs $139.99 and is available for preorder through LEGO's online store. LEGO is limiting 21370 E.T. purchases to three per customer, a standard anti-scalping measure for new releases that are expected to see significant demand.

The newly announced set also includes a built-in light brick that can be activated from the back, making E.T.'s heart glow. That is not to be confused with LEGO's Smart Play platform, which is a much more sophisticated system that integrates NFC sensors, speakers, and configurable lights into a single Smart Brick. By contrast, the 21370 E.T. set uses a simpler battery-powered component that emits a red light when switched on, mimicking the alien's glowing heart in its default configuration. Long before LEGO formally revealed the Smart Play platform in January 2026, the company had experimented with light-emitting bricks in sets such as 6783 Sonar Transmitting Cruiser, first released in 1986. The two LR41 batteries required to power E.T.'s heart are included in the package.

It was first submitted in April 2023 and took nearly two years to reach the mandatory 10,000-vote milestone required to qualify for a LEGO review. After being selected as an official Ideas product in October 2025, the set underwent an adaptation process led by LEGO's designers. The final model is remarkably similar to the original concept, with the differences mostly limited to specific piece choices, presumably to support easier manufacturing.

item.title: New Official Resident Evil Release Confirmed for July 30
item.description:
Resident Evil fans have a brand-new official release to look forward to on Thursday, July 30. The Resident Evil franchise has been on a ridiculous hot streak for nearly a decade. While Capcom definitely misstepped with Resident Evil 6 , Resident Evil 7 got things back on track and it's been nothing but bangers ever since when it comes to main series entries.

The latest main series Resident Evil game is Resident Evil Requiem , which launched earlier this year to rave reviews. Resident Evil Requiem reviews praised the game for expertly blending the slow-burn, first-person horror of RE7 with the explosive third-person action of games like Resident Evil 4 . Requiem is one of the highest-rated new game releases of 2026 so far, and it's readily available across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and even the Nintendo Switch 2.

Resident Evil Requiem Amiibo Release Date and Price

  • July 30
  • $29.99

Resident Evil Requiem 's Switch 2 port is especially interesting because it will soon be getting its own set of amiibo figures. Capcom has confirmed that the previously-announced Grace and Leon amiibo figures will be available on Thursday, July 30, with pre-orders live now. Scanning the amiibo figures will net players special weapon skins to use in the game, like the Neon skin for Grace's S&S M232, and a unique look for the titular Requiem magnum. The Resident Evil Requiem amiibo figures cost $29.99 each, but for hardcore fans of the franchise, they may very well be worth it.

The amiibo figures are highly-detailed, featuring Grace with her jacket and backpack and Leon wielding his trusty hatchet. The figures are likely going to be hard to come by, and in fact have already sold out at retailers like GameStop, and so fans should keep that in mind. The skins that they add to Resident Evil Requiem are unlikely to give anyone too much FOMO, but the figures are cool as collector's items by themselves.

As far as more substantial content goes, we do know that a Resident Evil Requiem story expansion is on the way. What we don't know is what form it will take or when it will be available. While some believed that the Resident Evil Requiem story DLC would be out by the end of the year, recent leaks and rumors have suggested it may launch after 2027's Resident Evil Veronica . Resident Evil Veronica is pegged for an early 2027 release, so that means fans may be waiting quite a long time for Resident Evil Requiem story DLC.

Resident Evil Veronica is the only one confirmed right now, but reputable leakers have claimed that a Resident Evil Zero remake is on the way, along with Resident Evil 10 . It's also been suggested that a second Resident Evil 1 remake is in the works, too, but again, none of these projects have been officially announced by Capcom at the time of this writing.

item.title: Diablo 4 Season 14 Nerfs Its Best Mythic
item.description:
With the launch of Diablo 4 Season 14 and its Mythic 3.0 update, what was once a top-tier Mythic item is now a shell of its former self. In an effort to rework how Mythic items work, Diablo 4 has changed Mythic from a rarity to a quality, giving all Uniques the potential to be Mythic. While this change comes with a 30% power boost to the item's Unique affix, some formerly Mythic-exclusive items, now called Iconic Mythics, got hit with nerfs to compensate.

Diablo 4 Season 14 has been off to a rocky start, with some fans taking issue with the overall reduced Mythic drop rate that wasn't mentioned in the Season 14 patch notes. This unexpected change makes obtaining Mythic Uniques under this new system even more of a hassle, and some of the builds that require Mythics to function are suffering as a result. Even if players can find an Iconic Mythic like the Heir of Perdition, they may not want to use it on their build after such a drastic nerf has made it far less viable than the alternatives.

Diablo 4 Season 14 Nerfs the Heir of Perdition Hard

In Diablo 4 Season 14, the Heir of Perdition's Unique Power is the target of a substantial nerf. Previously, the Iconic Mythic offered players a blanket 80% damage increase across the board, making it the clear best-in-slot helm for almost all Diablo 4 builds. However, that 80% damage increase is now a measly 15% blanket damage boost, making the Mythic Unique a far cry from the powerful helm it once was.

Heir of Perdition Mythic Ancestral Unique Helm 925 Item Power
Inherent: +200% Damage to Angels and Demons
+20% Critical Strike Chance +20% Lucky Hit Chance +20% Movement Speed +2 to Core Skills Give in to hatred and earn Lilith's Favor, increasing your damage dealt by 80%[x]. Slaughter enemies to briefly steal Lilith's Favor from Nearby allies. Beware false prophets donned as sheep yet bearing the stench of wolves. Thou shalt know them by their fruits. For a tree of good cannot produce evil, nor thorns yield a harvest sweet and fair.

Additionally, thanks to Mythics becoming a quality instead of a rarity, the Heir of Perdition doesn't come with the static affixes it did previously. While players are guaranteed a Primary Core Stat affix and a Movement Speed affix, neither of these is as useful as the previous version's guaranteed affixes. The bright side is that Diablo 4 players can re-roll the Mythic's other affixes in the Horadric Cube to get something better, like All Damage Multiplier or Critical Strike Damage Multiplier.

Even considering the 30% Unique Power boost to all Mythics, the Heir of Perdition is no longer the best-in-slot helm for Diablo 4 builds. On one hand, this opens the door for players to experiment with other gear on their Season 14 builds, potentially crafting a god-rolled Mythic in the Horadric Cube. Unfortunately, this change also means that the Heir of Perdition is unlikely to see much, if any, use this season.

The Heir of Perdition is one of the most interesting items in Diablo 4 from a lore perspective. It comes with an inherent affix that deals 200% damage to all Angels and Demons, which is strange given that there aren't any Angel enemies currently in the game. With Diablo 4 's Season of Death Awakening focusing on the Ullo Sar cult's plan to permanently connect Sanctuary with Pandemonium, some fans have theorized that Diablo 3: Reaper of Souls 's antagonist, the Angel Malthael, could be returning in Diablo 4 in the near future and would introduce Angel enemies for the Heir of Perdition to take advantage of.
